title: Overlord
content:
Rating: 8.5/10
Overlord stands out by telling the story from the perspective of the world's most powerful ruler instead of the hero. Ainz Ooal Gown is a fascinating protagonist whose intelligence and strategic thinking are just as impressive as his overwhelming strength. Combined with excellent world-building, memorable side characters, and political intrigue, Overlord delivers a unique take on the isekai genre because it does not follow the usual formula of a weak hero becoming powerful and saving the world.
Instead, it asks:
"What happens when the strongest being in the world is not the hero?"
The main character is morally grey, has very faithful subordinates, and can go extents for the welfare of him and his subordinates. Sometimes Ainz feel sorta dumb, but overall it feels amusing to watch him on screen.

title: Kuroko no Basket
content:
Kuroko no Basket takes the simple idea of basketball and turns it into an intense battle of talent, strategy, and determination. At first glance, it may look like a normal sports anime, but it quickly becomes a story about ambition, teamwork, rivalry, and the meaning of true strength.
The story follows Kuroko, a seemingly ordinary and unnoticed player who was once part of the legendary "Generation of Miracles"—a group of five extraordinary basketball players who dominated middle school basketball. Unlike his former teammates, Kuroko's strength is not raw power or skill, but his ability to support and bring out the best in others.
The arrival of Kagami, a talented and ambitious player with incredible physical abilities, creates the perfect contrast. Their partnership becomes the heart of the series: Kagami represents overwhelming individual talent, while Kuroko represents teamwork and strategy.
What I liked the most:
Every major opponent feels unique.
Matches are not just about scoring points; they are battles of mind games and different philosophies.
The Generation of Miracles are memorable because each one represents a different idea of basketball.
The rivalry between players keeps the story exciting.
Extremely hype matches.
Players with almost "superhuman" abilities (not realistic basketball).
Strong character development.
Tournament-style progression.
The story is about proving that basketball is a team sports and hardwork, passion, teamwork, can absolutely beat talent and arrogance.

title: The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Slums
content:
Rating: 8/10
The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Slums is a fun and relaxing fantasy anime with a likable overpowered protagonist. It balances comedy, action, and wholesome moments without taking itself too seriously. While the story is simple, the charming characters and satisfying main character moments make it an enjoyable binge.

title: Blue Lock
content:
Rating: 7/10
Rating: 8/10
Blue Lock offers a unique take on sports anime by focusing on individual ambition over teamwork. The intense matches, creative strategies, and constant competition keep the series engaging throughout. While some games feel stretched out, Isagi's development and the evolving rivalries make it an entertaining watch. Overall, it's a refreshing football anime with exciting moments and a strong premise.
There is a significant downgrade in animation quality in season 2 but the story is tight enough to keep one engaged. Moreover everything feels worth watching for the last episode of season 2.
Eagerly waiting for S3.
![](images/ms13f874.jpg)

title: Parasyte
content:
Rating: 9/10
Parasyte: The Maxim is much more than an action anime—it is a story about humanity, identity, and survival. Shinichi's transformation from an ordinary teenager into someone emotionally conflicted and mentally stronger was one of the best aspects of the series. His character development felt natural and meaningful.
What stood out the most was Migi. Rather than being a typical companion, Migi represented pure logic, making every decision based on reason rather than emotion. The contrast between Shinichi's humanity and Migi's rational thinking made the story thought-provoking.
The action was intense, but the emotional and philosophical themes left a much stronger impact. It constantly made me question what truly defines a human and whether monsters are always the ones who look different.
![](images/ms13406r.jpg)
Overall, Parasyte delivers an engaging story with memorable characters, meaningful themes, and excellent pacing, making it a highly enjoyable watch.

title: Life Lately
content:
Watched Akame Ga Kill
Rating: 8.5/10
Akame ga Kill! stayed true to its premise from start to finish. Despite the title, the story is really Tatsumi's journey. He was never the strongest character, but his growth from an emotional, reckless boy into a capable warrior was well written and believable.
Every member of Night Raid had a unique role, making every loss emotionally impactful. What I appreciated most was the moral complexity—while some characters fighting for the Empire were truly evil, others had genuine beliefs and reasons for their actions.
With only 24 episodes and little to no filler, the series delivers a complete story about a rebellion against a corrupt government, backed by exciting action, memorable characters, and great power systems. Overall, it was an engaging and highly enjoyable watch.
